# Private hosted wallet market

An additive, money-off adapter composed with the existing SDS contributor journey. Root receives the final feature exports and performs any real installation. The ROOT186 source and receipts remain at `5683f40c`; ROOT191 results are in `ROOT191-RECEIVING.md` and `evidence/root191/`.

The existing account, claim, submission, review, terms and obligation engines remain authoritative. Opportunity obligations stay in `opportunity_obligations`; no matching row is fabricated in the main earned-work ledger. Earned-work obligations are supported through their own accepted source. The 5% fee applies only to newly quoted market work, never to original earned obligations.

The installed HTTP consumer has contract version3. It requires Root owner authentication, a persisted enrollment of the complete source/host closure, profile/store/RPC binding, an already received Root registry allocation/discharge, the actual accepted store source and exact canonical finalized Base/USDC transfer. SQL stores an append-only paid projection of that existing allocation. It cannot issue a payment or a second transfer allocation. The archival obligation remains owed, and the existing authenticated native review reports paid through its existing canonical qualification interface.

The bundled canonical sender module and pure retained-award validator exactly match Pilot `84a6c5bdd459f4a670951b722020b2b57fe1ae81`; `contracts/source-lineage.json` records their hashes. The sender's default import contract remains unbound. Public flags, a raw client, a descriptor, a supplied baseline, RPC or installation boolean cannot bind it. The installed server constructs its consumer from its closed-over profile and persistent store.

The SDS artifact includes the adapter, SQL, source contracts, admin command and declared `pg` dependency. It resolves its entry relative to itself and refuses external checkout paths and escaping symlinks. Existing contributor session/review routes retain their consumer. The maintained packed client's `c0-1` header selects its routes; private debt administration uses the owner-only native-debt routes. Direct TLS or the existing contributor ingress guard protects those routes. Anonymous market discovery is empty with public reads off. Public health omits the database hostname and RPC URL.

Private-chain funding retains the existing payer signature, stored intent, quote expiry, exact token/source/recipient/gross, proof uniqueness and replay checks. Public chains refuse funding, funding intents and capture. No signing/broadcast endpoint is added. The maintained client456 source commit remains `480c8199629fa4b35bc05e878b640d3fb9442b50`. The packed archive at `client/agent-economy-client-0.1.0.tgz`, sha256 `6c1186e6f0e5f4bfbbfa3887a0c0df728f51c6dff8605c9cfe0d6cf3e069b1e3`, is that client plus the read-only `ae task retained` command. Every packed member matches the worktree client. The older Root53 archive remains historical. The maintained `ae task intent` and `account resume` commands stay in the archive; ERC-1271 and EIP-712 remain unsupported.

Run `npm test` in this directory with the exact SDS fixture inputs named in the receiving receipt. The separate `test/opportunity-receiving.mts` uses the unchanged Neo input's installed fixture and the actual compiled SDS runtime over verified TLS PostgreSQL. It exercises real signup/claim/submission/requester acceptance, distinct financial reservation, paid review readback, a differently valued second obligation, equally funded wrong-source refusal, native SQL uniqueness and restart/rollback retention. The test fixtures do not qualify a live installation.

`INSTALL-ROLLBACK.md` is the current private recipe. It preserves the current full environment, existing debts, allocations, recoverable operations and main auto-deploy=false. Production rollback disables code without dropping durable state. Human/public publication, live enrollment and money movement remain Root's actions.
